summary: Defines the LDAP Proxied Authorization Control. It lets a client ask that an operation be processed under a given authorization identity instead of the one tied to the current connection. It is standards-track.

plainLanguage.summary: The LDAP Proxy Authorization Control lets a client ask the server to process one operation as a specified identity. The server checks its own policy before allowing the request.

questions: what is the ldap proxied authorization control
what does ldap result code 123 mean
subtitle: An LDAP control for requesting one operation under a specified authorization identity.

tldr.problem: An authorization identity bound to an entire LDAP session is less convenient for a client acting for multiple users.
tldr.mechanism: A control carries an authorization identity for a single request and must have its criticality flag set to TRUE.
tldr.outcome: The server executes the request as that identity only when its policy allows the client to adopt it; otherwise it returns result code 123.

today: RFC 4370 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Authorization Identity for One Operation
sections.content:
LDAP can use SASL to supply an authorization identity that applies to an entire session. The Proxy Authorization Control lets a client specify an identity for an individual operation, which can help clients acting on behalf of multiple users.

A server advertises support by including the control's object identifier, 2.16.840.1.113730.3.4.18, in its root DSE supportedControl attribute.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of changing the identity for a whole connection, a client can request a different identity for one operation.

sections.title: Control Requirements
sections.content:
A single Proxy Authorization Control can accompany a search, compare, modify, add, delete, modify DN, or extended operation request, with exceptions for extensions that change authentication, authorization, or confidentiality.

The control's criticality flag MUST be present and TRUE. Its value MUST contain an authorization identity or be empty for an anonymous association. A server MUST reject a missing or false criticality flag with a protocolError.
sections.plainLanguage: The client must mark the control as required. This prevents a request from silently running under the wrong identity if the server cannot honor it.

sections.title: Server Policy and Security
sections.content:
The server's proxy-authorization policy determines whether the client may adopt an identity. If the identity is recognized and the client is authorized, the operation is processed as if submitted by that identity. Otherwise the server returns result code 123.

The control can be sent over secure or insecure channels. Authorization identities may contain confidential information, and the RFC says anonymous users SHOULD NOT be allowed to assume another identity.
sections.plainLanguage: The server decides whether the client may act as the named identity. It should not allow anonymous users to act as other people.
